In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in the newborn mammal, the hormonal control of the development and the maintenance of gluconeogenesis is a complex phenomenon, involving the interaction of several hormones and the participation of many other factors.
the neonatal liver is not a miniature adult organ, but a distinct organ with its own specific features and regulatory mechanisms.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in the newborn mammal, the liver is a major site for gluconeogenesis and that this process is controlled by the hormonal milieu.

, in newborn mammals, the hormonal environment is a major determinant of hepatic glucoeogenesis, and that, in addition, a number of metabolic factors are required to maintain a high hepatic gluconeogenic capacity.
the hormonal control of gluconeogenesis is similar in the neonatal rat, the newborn lamb and the human newborn.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, at birth, the neonatal liver is not yet prepared to deal with a postnatal diet rich in fat and poor in glucose.
the neonate is a unique model of the adult, and the neonatal period is an ideal time for studying the hormonal regulation of hepatic glucose metabolism in the adult.
